items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: I was playing at the Apollo Theater with Quincy Jones

ctx.x: Oh, yeah, going back to that story with the Chesterfield story and, you know, taking that case up to the union. While -- it reminds me of other stuff, too. First, while we were at the union these guys were saying, well, it's not that we're prejudiced against the black guys. But you know how it is, the black guy's a jazz musician, he can't read. And, you know, they're troublemakers. And Feinberg said, "Well, I've got a white, Anglo-Saxon man sitting here, Protestant -- he didn't know I'm not a protestant, who…

So repercussions went on through the years but the nicest one was 20 years later, I was playing at the Apollo Theater with Quincy Jones and Redd Foxx was the star, Billy Eckstine and Redd Foxx. And the last night -- well, Redd Foxx always kidded me, looked back and called me "The Lord," because
I had long hair. He said, "I knew everything was all right when I saw the Lord back there in the trumpet section."
